LABEL: concept
Question: s the term primarily abstract or theoretical? Does the term refer to a scientific or mathematical concept rather than something that exists in the system being described? Is the term a statistical term, theoretical framework, methodological construct?
Examples: statistical terms, theoretical frameworks, methodological constructs, normal distribution, regression, resilience (in theoretical discussion), binomial distribution, theory, record, pattern
Definition: abstract or theoretical construct used in analysis or discourse (e.g. climate, conservation status, resilience, scenario, vulnerability, link, trend, normal distribution, regression, resilience, binomial distribution, theory)

LABEL: temporal entity
Question: Does the term refer to time periods, temporal units, or temporal attributes? Is it a time unit or a time interval?
Examples: breeding season, monsoon, Holocene, winter, season, fire season, year, epoch
Definition: a named or identifiable time period or phase

LABEL: temporal property
Question: Does the term refer to time periods, temporal units, or temporal attributes? Is it a temporal attribute?
Examples: annual, decadal, phenological timing, duration, diel, interannual variability, short term, first time, prior

LABEL: spatial entity
Question: Does the term describe a place, spatial unit, location, or spatial extent? Is it a place or a spatial unit? Can I point to it?
Examples: watershed, grid cell, elevation belt, buffer zone, district, national park, grid cell, polygon
Definition: a named or operational geographic extent or geometric unit used for mapping or aggregation, a geographic location that could appear on a map or have a bounding box

LABEL: spatial property
Question: Does the term describe a place, spatial unit, location, or spatial extent? Is it a spatial attribute, Is this a value I would measure or a direction/relative position?
Examples: elevation, slope, aspect, distance, area, location, perimeter, spatial extent, distance to road, windward side, eastern slopes
Definition: a geometric or positional descriptor of a location

LABEL: anthropogenic entity
Question: Is the phenomenon created, performed, or organized by humans? Is it a human-created thing?
Examples: road, dam, house, mine, bank, land-tenure regime, law, management plan, traditional knowledge, conservation policy, family, emergence trap, strategies
Definition: a human-made physical object, infrastructure or modification
Comment: a human-made physical or intellectual object, infrastructure or modification or knowledge

LABEL: anthropogenic process
Question: Is the phenomenon created, performed, or organized by humans? Is it a human activity or action?
Examples: mining, policy implementation, conservation planning, human migration, irrigation, logging, deforestation, tourism, surveys, patrols, work
Definition: an activity or action performed by humans that affects socioecological systems, process nominalizations that refer to an activity or plan in progress
Comment: Human research activity (e.g. analysis, sampling, measurement, etc) is usually part of the methods section and we do not label it

LABEL: anthropogenic property
Question: Is the phenomenon created, performed, or organized by humans? Is it a characteristic of human systems?
Examples: population density, land tenure type, ownership, infrastructure density, tourism pressure, literacy rate
Definition: a measurable social, economic or governance attribute

LABEL: abiotic entity
Question: Does the term refer to non-living environmental phenomena? Does it refer to a physical thing or substance or aggregated environmental system?
Examples: rock, glacier, soil, river, moraine, mountain, permafrost layer, rock outcrop, snowpack, lake OR glacial deposits, soil horizons, sediment layers
Definition: a non-living natural physical object or component of the environment, or an aggregation or assemblage of abiotic entities forming a functional unit

LABEL: abiotic process
Question: Does it refer to an environmental process?
Examples: erosion, landsliding, glacial melt, climate change, climate warming, condensation, convection, orographic uplift, wind drift, thermal inversion, orogeny, avalanche, sedimentation, soil sealing
Definition: a physical or chemical change in the environment

LABEL: abiotic property
Question: Does it refer to an environmental attribute?
Examples: climatic condition, cold climate, mean global temperature, salinity, snow cover, conductivity, radiation, abiotic environmental factors, pH
Definition: a measurable physical or chemical attribute

LABEL: biotic entity
Question: Does the term involve living organisms or biological material? Does it refer to a single organism or biological object OR Does it correspond to a group of organisms functioning together?
Examples: snow leopard, juniper species, species (e.g. we reported this species for the first time), rhododendron, plants, ruminants, stem, organ, Vulpes vulpes, tetra chamois, leaf OR community, guild, ecosystem, fauna, mixed broadleaf forest, population, alpine grassland, vegetation layers, predator-prey system, riparian vegetation, species (e.g. carnivorous species are dangerous)
Definition: a living organism or taxon at the individual/species level  OR an assemblage of organisms functioning as a unit

LABEL: biotic process
Question: Does it refer to a biological activity or interaction?
Examples: pollination, predation, succession, migration, decomposition, flowering, disappearance of species, population decrease, herbivory, phenology, nutrient cycling
Definition: a biological action or interaction performed by or involving living organisms

LABEL: biotic property
Question: Is it an attribute of organisms or biological systems?
Examples: biomass, species richness, forest biodiversity, population growth rate, genetic diversity, habitat condition, canopy height, wood density, functional trait
Definition: a trait, attribute or measurable characteristic of organisms or biotic assemblages

LABEL: quantitative property
Question: Can it be measured or counted?
Examples: 16%, 100 meters above the sea level, 3000 km, 15 species, half of a populations
Definition: a measurable attribute of an object

LABEL: qualitative property
Question: What kind is this entity/process/property from the point of its unmeasurable attributes? Can it be characterised?
Examples: Big mountain, fast change, unpredictable growth,
